## Exact assumptions and conditional bounds

- [`sat26-sparse`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-sparse)
- [`sat26-reported-formal`](../../ASSUMPTIONS.md#sat26-reported-formal)

Conditional on `sat26-sparse`:

$$
2^{O(m/\sqrt{\log m})}L^{O(1)}
$$

Alternatively, conditional on `sat26-reported-formal`:

$$
2^{O(m(\log\log m)^2/\sqrt{\log m})}L^{O(1)}
$$

The resulting algorithm is deterministic and uses polynomial space, conditional on the corresponding assumption and this derivation. $L$ denotes the original input length; constants may depend on the stated fixed constants. Logarithms in asymptotic bounds may be regularized when the declared measure is small.

## Preprocessing

Intersect each degree interval with [0,deg_G(v)], returning zero if empty. Check isolated vertices separately; then discard them.

## Encoding size

| Quantity | Bound |
| --- | --- |
| Boolean variables, including auxiliaries | $O(m)$ |
| Clauses | $O(m)$ |
| Maximum clause width | $3$ |

## Derivation

1. Use one bit for each edge. At vertex v sum the incident bits using O(deg_G(v)) gates, then compare with the clipped lower and upper bounds.

2. The comparisons cost O(log(deg_G(v)+1)) gates at nonisolated vertices, so the entire circuit has O(m) gates. Equivalence encodings give one auxiliary extension per edge subset.

3. Thus O(m) variables and 3-clauses suffice, and the sparse counting profile applies. Reading even very long input bounds contributes only to the polynomial input-length factor.

## Caveats and comparison limits

- Includes all matchings, b-matchings, perfect matchings, edge covers, f-factors, and 2-factors through local degree bounds. These are applications of one shared argument.
- A 2-factor need not be connected. This does not count Hamiltonian cycles.
- The bounds are degree constraints, not arbitrary objective weights on edges.

Counting requires a count-preserving encoding and preprocessing, or an explicit correction for multiplicities. The derivation must justify this; decision preservation alone is insufficient.
